correctness.rationale: PASS — For n>=3 on the Euclidean zero-sum unit sphere, the standard translated zonotope equals sum_{i<j}[e_i,e_j], so directional width is W=sum|u_i−u_j|. On any strict coordinate-order chamber W=<a,u>, where a_j=2j−n−1 and ||a||²=n(n²−1)/3; the only compatible spherical stationary maximum is normalized a, yielding n! strict global maxima. On two-level partitions A/A^c with t=|A|, W=sqrt(n t(n−t)); sorting any mean-zero m-vector and decomposing into monotone cut steps gives sharp within-block inequality T_m(z)>=sqrt(m(m−1))||z||. Tangents separately sum zero on both blocks; before tan θ < delta/sqrt(2) no cross-order changes, giving attained lower envelope W(theta)=sqrt(n t(n−t)) cos θ+gamma sin θ (gamma least nontrivial block sqrt(m(m−1))), proving strict local minima and exact slope. For >=3 distinct value levels, restriction to their positive-dimensional ordered block-constant stratum has no local minimum; splitting a repeated block increases W so no local maximum. Exhausts all extrema; smallest t=1 or n−1 give 2n global minima. Independent direct exact-numerical geodesics n,t=(7,3),(8,1),(5,2) reproduce sharp envelope to 1e−11. Global theorem rests on analytic proof, not finite diagnostics.
